explainers.name: Attention Is All You Need (Gemini 3.8 Flash, 2026-10-22 evaluation)

explainer.summary: Sequence transduction models relied on recurrent or convolutional architectures whose sequential computation limited parallelization and made learning distant dependencies hard. The authors introduce the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture based entirely on self-attention and feed-forward sub-layers with positional encodings. It achieves state-of-the-art translation performance with 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French at significantly reduced training cost.

background.name: Encoder-Decoder Architecture
background.line: A sequence modeling framework mapping an input sequence to continuous representations and decoding symbols auto-regressively; the Transformer retains this high-level structure.

background.name: Recurrent and Convolutional Sequence Models
background.line: Networks processing tokens sequentially or across sliding receptive fields; the paper identifies their sequential bottlenecks and long path lengths as the key limitation to overcome.

background.name: Attention Mechanisms
background.line: Mechanisms that map a query and key-value pairs to a weighted sum of values; the paper extends this concept into self-attention to dispense with recurrence entirely.

background.name: Residual Connections and Layer Normalization
background.line: Techniques for stabilizing gradient flow across deep networks; applied around every attention and feed-forward sub-layer in the encoder and decoder stacks.

ideas.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
ideas.line: A fast matrix-based attention function that divides dot products by the square root of key dimension to prevent gradient vanishing in the softmax.

ideas.name: Multi-Head Attention
ideas.line: Linearly projects queries, keys, and values into multiple representation subspaces in parallel, counteracting the resolution loss of single-head averaging.

ideas.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
ideas.line: Fixed sinusoid functions of varying frequencies added to embeddings to inject token sequence order without recurrence or convolutions.

ideas.name: The Transformer Architecture
ideas.line: A stacked architecture combining multi-head self-attention, encoder-decoder attention, and position-wise feed-forward networks within residual blocks.

ideas.name: State-of-the-Art Translation with Faster Training
ideas.line: Achieved 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French, outperforming prior models at a fraction of their training cost.

explainers.text:
Sequence transduction models relied on recurrent or convolutional architectures whose sequential computation limited parallelization and made learning distant dependencies hard. The authors introduce the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture based entirely on self-attention and feed-forward sub-layers with positional encodings. It achieves state-of-the-art translation performance with 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French at significantly reduced training cost.

Background:
- Encoder-Decoder Architecture: A sequence modeling framework mapping an input sequence to continuous representations and decoding symbols auto-regressively; the Transformer retains this high-level structure.
- Recurrent and Convolutional Sequence Models: Networks processing tokens sequentially or across sliding receptive fields; the paper identifies their sequential bottlenecks and long path lengths as the key limitation to overcome.
- Attention Mechanisms: Mechanisms that map a query and key-value pairs to a weighted sum of values; the paper extends this concept into self-attention to dispense with recurrence entirely.
- Residual Connections and Layer Normalization: Techniques for stabilizing gradient flow across deep networks; applied around every attention and feed-forward sub-layer in the encoder and decoder stacks.

Key ideas:
- Scaled Dot-Product Attention: A fast matrix-based attention function that divides dot products by the square root of key dimension to prevent gradient vanishing in the softmax.
- Multi-Head Attention: Linearly projects queries, keys, and values into multiple representation subspaces in parallel, counteracting the resolution loss of single-head averaging.
- Sinusoidal Positional Encoding: Fixed sinusoid functions of varying frequencies added to embeddings to inject token sequence order without recurrence or convolutions.
- The Transformer Architecture: A stacked architecture combining multi-head self-attention, encoder-decoder attention, and position-wise feed-forward networks within residual blocks.
- State-of-the-Art Translation with Faster Training: Achieved 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French, outperforming prior models at a fraction of their training cost.
